overview: This one-page file consists of a 1930 list of papers concerning lime and cement in Japan. It indexes two diplomatic reports by Neville: an April telegram on the unsatisfactory condition of the Japanese cement industry, and an August cross-reference to a report that the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau had considered rationalizing the Cement Federation and cement industry, including a possible merger of companies. The sheet directs researchers to related decimal-file records rather than reproducing the underlying reports.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomatic officer in Japan; sender of the referenced telegrams

subfiles.title: List of papers on lime and cement in Japan
subfiles.about: An index sheet identifies two diplomatic reports concerning the condition and proposed rationalization of Japan's cement industry.
subfiles.summary: The first entry, dated August 1, points to a report by Neville that the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau considered rationalization of the Cement Federation and the wider cement industry, including a merger of companies. The second entry, dated April 7, refers to Neville's telegram 107, which described the cement industry's present condition as unsatisfactory despite indications that it was supposedly in good condition. The sheet supplies cross-references to other decimal-file records, including 694.00 P.R./32 and 694.50/62.

interest: The sheet is useful chiefly as an archival roadmap linking otherwise dispersed State Department records about Japanese cement production. Its brief entries capture contemporary concern with overcapacity or poor industrial conditions and show that government-sponsored rationalization and corporate consolidation were already under discussion in 1930. It also illustrates how economic intelligence moved through the State Department's decimal filing system and how a single subject file could depend heavily on cross-references to related classifications.
